summary.headline: Choice International Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to Rs 379 crore and PAT rose 23% to Rs 69-70 crore, a record quarter.
summary.overview: Management reported record consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 379 crore (up 33% YoY from Rs 284 crore), EBITDA of about Rs 131 crore (34.5% margin) and PAT of about Rs 70 crore (18.3% margin, up 23%). Broking and distribution and advisory each contributed roughly half of revenue, with NBFC at about 12%. The company completed a Rs 900 crore NH Investment & Securities investment in the broking arm via CCPS, announced a 1:1 bonus issue, and moved the Feedback Infra acquisition forward with a Letter of Intent from the Resolution Professional. Management flagged regulatory risk to insurance commissions and NBFC funding costs after the repo hike. Note that the call cites PAT as Rs 69 crore in one place and about Rs 70 crore in another.

segments.name: Broking and distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 178 crore and PBT about Rs 42 crore; 218 branches, client assets and custody Rs 66,300 crore, ADTO down 12% QoQ in line with market. MTF book Rs 463 crore. Wealth AUM about Rs 6,000 crore (MF Rs 4,100 crore, PMS/AIF Rs 291 crore).

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 145 crore and PBT about Rs 45 crore, supported by five mainboard and SME IPOs (about Rs 680 crore issue size). Government advisory order book Rs 710 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore and PBT about Rs 4 crore; total loan book Rs 935 crore. Margins hit by microfinance stress over recent quarters, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 20% ROE and aims to maintain it.
Customer growth of about 30-40% in tier 3 and beyond geographies; MTF-led activity expected to add about 10 percentage points to overall growth rate.
Pipeline of 24 IPO mandates with estimated fundraise of Rs 6,210 crore; at least four to five IPOs expected in H2 FY27.

Feedback Infra expected to become part of Choice in about the next quarter, subject to NCLT approval; existing order book Rs 300 crore-plus, with about Rs 200 crore-plus of order book to be added post acquisition.
FY30 target advisory mix of roughly 50:50 between government advisory and investment banking.
H2 priorities: StrikeX adoption, new digital products, MTF expansion using NH capital, NCD and fixed income distribution, AMC active schemes.
capex_capacity: Rs 900 crore NH Investment & Securities CCPS investment completed in Choice Equity Broking; end use is mixed (MTF, settlement funding, capex, working capital) with no segregation given.
MTF book Rs 463 crore; management says deployment of the NH money began after 27 October and expects it to be deployed in the current quarter.
Feedback Infra acquisition pending NCLT approval; Letter of Intent received from Resolution Professional after Committee of Creditors approval.
Choice Large and Midcap Fund (first actively managed AMC scheme) NFO closed on the day of the call; collection figures to be shared shortly.
demand_pricing: Product distribution (structured and fixed income) reached Rs 1,636 crore in H1 FY27 versus Rs 512 crore a year earlier and above full-year FY26 volume of Rs 745 crore.
IPO fees generally 3% to 8-9% of issue size depending on sector and company; management sees no major margin pressure.
Wealth AUM yield of about 60-75 bps; management says regulators are unlikely to cut commissions materially.
Insurance: proposed commission and distribution-expense changes could pressure intermediary revenue, depending on final framework and product mix.
Market context: MTF industry book moderated from about Rs 1.6 lakh crore to Rs 1.5 lakh crore by October end; RBI repo rose from 5.25% to 5.50% in October.
India Post Payments Bank pilot: over 25,000 customers and AUM of about Rs 1.12 crore in roughly 38 days; revenue impact too early to assess.

qa_highlights.question: Demat accounts are up 14% but active accounts are flat; what is holding back activation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dormant accounts are a result of the NSE 12-month active UCC rule, and a dedicated team is working on reactivation through portfolio alerts and research reports.

qa_highlights.question: How do CBA-sourced revenues compare with direct digital clients in payout and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: CBAs are treated as branch originators, and payouts range from 15% to 40% depending on product; CBA and branch revenue cannot be separated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and impact of the Feedback Infra acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Resolution plan approved by CoC; NCLT hearing pending. Management expects margin improvement from larger projects and about Rs 200 crore-plus of order book to be added after acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on tier 3 and beyond cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited under-penetration, higher lifetime customer value from physical distribution, and a 30-40% customer growth target in these geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IPO fee and H2 IPO pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees range from 3% to 8-9%; management did not disclose SEBI observation status and expects at least four to five IPOs in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the terms and timeline for NH's CCPS conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion is about three years away and the ratio is not yet fixed, pending conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 146 crore advisory revenue sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said advisory revenue depends on the number of IPOs during the quarter, and government consulting remains at about Rs 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 MTF income exceed Rs 100 crore given the NH capital deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MTF revenue will be added as the book grows and expects deployment in the current quarter; no explicit Q3 number was given.

risks_watch: Insurance commission and distribution-expense reform could compress intermediary revenue.
NBFC microfinance stress and funding-cost repricing after the October repo hike; management expects microfinance revival but gave no timeline.
Dormant client base (active accounts flat while demat accounts rise 14%) and ADTO down 12% QoQ.
Feedback Infra completion pending NCLT approval; execution risk on integration.
IPO market dependence: advisory revenue swings with IPO count, and the 24-mandate pipeline has no disclosed filing or observation status.
Pace of MTF deployment of the Rs 900 crore NH capital, and the ability to lift returns on that capital.
Undisclosed regulatory impact of SEBI CAS proposal; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and pipeline, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give several numbers (IPO filings, AMC collections, CAS impact) and gave qualitative answers on insurance regulation and the timing of MTF revenue.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was the strongest quarter in our history, with a revenue of Rs. 379 crores, up to 33% YoY basis, and PAT of Rs. 69 crore, up 23% YoY basis.
Product distribution reaches Rs. 1,636 crore in H1 FY27, over three times the year-ago level and more than double the full year FY26 volume.
We have put the money to use after 27th October. So, it's almost been a week only.
On the ROE numbers, we are expecting close to around 20% ROE, which we will expect to maintain.
